collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager interpreting for a deaf neighbor in a heated fence argument has gone quiet: translate word for word, or politely.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is deaf and is having a disagreement with (neighbor), a neighbor, about a fence. (friend), who signs well, has been asked to interpret. The disagreement is getting heated. (subject) has just signed something, quite fast and with a lot of feeling, and (friend) has gone very quiet.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) says, "(subject.He/she) disagrees strongly." (subject), watching (friend)'s lips, signs immediately: "That is NOT what I said." (friend) sighs and translates the goat part too. (neighbor) is offended. Then (neighbor) looks at the goat. "...Fine." The fence gets moved. (subject) tells (friend) never to tidy up (subject.his/her) words again.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) takes a deep breath and says it out loud, exactly: "(subject.He/she) says your fence is uglier than your goat, and your goat is the ugliest animal on Isola." There's a terrible silence. Then (neighbor) bursts out laughing. "That's fair, actually. It is a very ugly goat." The argument goes much better after that.
